# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s143, seat A) | **KS-858/F5 fix READY (#884 @ `f3a037978`) + the AUTHORISED DEMO PROBE** — 2026-09-07 06:15→06:51 AEST; option A built and measured against Wednesday's GO/NO-GO criterion, then Kam's one-probe authorisation executed at minimum cost | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It designed the probe so the measurement cost two read-only GETs.** Kam authorised ONE read-only probe of a LIVE box and forbade exhausting a limiter. Rather than drive a counter, it noticed every mount sets `standardHeaders: true` and that **the `RateLimit-Policy` VALUE names which limiter answered** — so the answer is readable without touching a ceiling. It then chose the route by SAFETY, reasoning explicitly past login (lockout counters + a credential-stuffing signature in the client's logs), register (creates accounts), forgot-password (mails a real person) and `/api/users/me/mfa` (needs a bearer → a credential → Wednesday's stop rule), landing on `verify-email` **because `app.use` matches every method, so a GET traverses the limiter mount exactly as a POST does.** Result: canonical `100;w=900`, double-slash `2000;w=60`; **no path-scoped mount on that box has a 60s window** — enumerated, not sampled — so the miss is unambiguous. **F5 is LIVE on the demo, 300x more permissive on that route.** Both requests 404'd at the backend; nothing written, no credential sent, no limiter exhausted. `server: nginx` on both also settled that neither Caddy nor the compose nginx collapses the path inbound. **And it disclosed that its OWN pre-stated condition would have given the opposite answer.** Its NULL bucket read *"not live — BOTH spellings carry the headers"*; both DID, because a different limiter answered and supplied headers of its own. **Read literally, its own condition said CLEAN.** It reported the raw values anyway — the brief required it — saw they contradicted its bucket, and named the instrument failure rather than re-filing quietly: *"if I had recorded only a pass/fail against my stated condition, this probe would have returned a confident false negative and Kam's message would have said the demo was clean."* It also refused to widen the authorisation to the other seven mounts and marked them **inference, not measurement**, and separated the measured limiter-miss from the UNMEASURED question of whether the demo would serve a POST through `//`. **Earlier the same session, on the fix:** 32 of 32 already-canonical rows identical across every mount class the gateway declares (enumerated, because Wednesday's criterion makes an unmeasurable case a NO-GO), 4/4 query rows byte-identical, 8/8 limiter mounts firing on `//` each with its own distinct 429 as a positive control, the KS-843 gdpr shape closed on all four spellings, and the double-apply measured inert rather than assumed. **It caught a contaminated BEFORE that would have produced a false NO-GO on its own correct fix** and took two fresh boots — then named the general defect in Wednesday's criterion: a safety tie-breaker has no control on the safe side. **It re-measured seat B's backend-404 claim itself rather than relaying it** (*"that claim was load-bearing for 'no new reachability', so it should not have travelled as someone else's"*). **And it refused an unexecutable Wednesday instruction** — "re-price KS-946 to Blocker" — establishing that the board has no such label and KS-946 is already at the top of the scale, rather than inventing a severity taxonomy. It flagged that automation (not its triage) walked two tickets, correct in substance, because its predecessor's trailers had walk
